subject: Geo transit capacity handshake — US/EU/APAC sizing and deal-trigger lanes
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc:
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft proposal — transitional transit lanes + region handoff for BlueHarbor

Team,

BlueHarbor just pushed an updated forecast (attached) and they want a hybrid dedicated plan: sustained US + EU pools, with APAC burst lanes and an explicit transit "handshake" for cross-region fallbacks. They care about predictable latency for EU customers and cost guarantees for the US-heavy portion of traffic.

Key asks from BlueHarbor:
- Committed US dedicated pool (m6-s equivalency/peak 1.2k RPS)
- EU committed pool with lower concurrency, but strict p99 latency
- APAC burst lanes for weekday spikes (Singapore primary)
- Clear deal triggers: when usage hits X for 3 consecutive weeks, move Y capacity from burst->committed

Irene — can you sketch a proposal for how we model the transit handshake (cold-warm node handoff + KV-cache warming) and what minimum buffer we should hold in each region? Lauren/Rishi — can you flag commercial and SLA implications if we include a hard trigger that converts burst to committed capacity mid-quarter?

Attached: BlueHarbor_demand-profile_Q2-Q4.xlsx (traffic by region + token mix)
Draft SOW will follow.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft proposal — transitional transit lanes + region handoff for BlueHarbor

Thanks — reviewed the demand file quickly. High level notes and a sizing sketch:  

1) Handoff model (recommended):
- Maintain a small warm standby (KV-prefetch) in each region representing ~6% of steady-state committed capacity. This lets us avoid cold-start penalty when failing over to a fallback pool.
- Transit handshake: route-first-token to local pool, concurrently warm a subset of KV slots in destination pool (30s warm window) then shift steady stream once warming reaches threshold.

2) Sizing numbers (ballpark, can refine with perf curves):
- US committed: hold capacity for 1.25k RPS peak (equiv. 8 x A100-80GB sustained slices) + 10% safety buffer = recommend reserving 9 slices.
- EU committed: 350 RPS sustained (3 slices) with tighter p99 SLO; use smaller batch sizes and prefer lower-quantization preserves latency.
- APAC burst lanes: configure 6 slices in burst pool with autoscale to 10 slices for extreme spikes; set warm-standby of 1 slice in SG region to reduce first-request p99.

3) Deal-trigger automation:
- Trigger rule: when average weekly tokens/requests per region exceed 85% of committed capacity for 3 consecutive weeks -> auto-notify sales + ops and create a tentative addendum reservation (7-day cooling before enforced billing change).
- Ops needs a manual approval window before converting burst to committed (to verify infra availability / procurement).

4) Operational impacts:
- Cross-region KV warming adds token overhead: expect ~3–6% extra cost for warm events; include in unit economics.
- We should reserve a 2-day capacity buffer for planned migrations or node maintenance per region.

I'll prepare a simple simulation (per-minute RPS -> slice count) and a table mapping token rates to slices. If we agree on the trigger and buffer, I can codify the autoscale policy and add an ops runbook.

Irene

--
Irene Choi
Product - Capacity & Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Jade Park <jade@blueharbor.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 00:22:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Draft proposal — transitional transit lanes + region handoff for BlueHarbor

Dylan,

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Irene's sizing looks reasonable and aligns with our internal sims. A few clarifications from our side before we move SOW draft to procurement: 

- For the EU committed pool: p99 latency requirement is 250ms for inference-only endpoints (not embeddings). Will the 3-slice recommendation meet that assuming A100-like perf?
- For the trigger flow: BlueHarbor needs a 14-day notice window before any committed-billing change takes effect. We can accept a 7-day tentative addendum if you keep it non-billable until confirmed after 14 days.
- APAC bursts: request that Redwood guarantee burst-to-committed availability for Singapore within 48 hours of request during onboarding ramp (we expect a few big spikes during our beta).

Also attaching a short procurement checklist — procurement@blueharbor.ai will open a DocuSign once we have the SOW + finalized numbers.

Cheers,
Jade

Attachments: BlueHarbor_procurement_checklist.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jade Park <jade@blueharbor.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft proposal — transitional transit lanes + region handoff for BlueHarbor

Jade — thanks, noted. Short answers and next steps: 

- EU p99: We'll validate with perf runs but initial mapping assumes A100-equivalent slices with lower batch sizes; Irene will run a p99 simulation and report back by EOD Fri. If we miss 250ms we will propose an SLA credit structure rather than more slices to keep price efficient.
- Trigger window: we can adopt your 14-day non-billable confirmation window. Ops will create the tentative addendum and mark it non-billable until BlueHarbor confirms after 14 days.
- APAC availability: agree to the 48-hour provisioning SLA during onboarding ramp; ops will reserve a standby tranche for the first 60 days post-go-live.

Action owners: 
- Irene: p99 simulation & per-region slice->cost table (deliverable: 2027-04-30 EOD)
- Lauren: update SOW language to include 14-day non-billable confirmation and APAC 48-hr ramp SLA (deliverable: 2027-05-01)
- Rishi: price impact analysis for standby tranches and warm-warm handshake cost adders (deliverable: 2027-04-30)
- Dylan: coordinate docsend + open HubSpot deal task for procurement (I'll attach SOW draft once Lauren has updated wording).

I'll attach the draft SOW and the demand file to the HubSpot deal: HubSpotDeal: 6789123.

Thanks team — seems like a tight but solvable set of asks.

Dylan
